To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we identified a mosaic mutation in a gene (ABCC8) encoding a potassium channel in a patient who presented with atypical diffuse hyperinsulinism, which is a condition characterized by abnormal insulin production.

we identified a novel genetic mechanism that explains atypical histological forms of congenital hyperinsulinaemia due to mosaic uniparenteral disomy in patients with dominatly inherited ATP-sensitive potassium channel gene (ABCC8 or KCNJ11) mutations.
we have identified a mosaic ABCC8 gene Q54X mutation and mosaic UPD for chromosome 11, resulting in atypical histological features of diffuse CHI.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the molecular mechanisms underlying the pathogenesis of CHI.

the genetic basis of congenital hyperinsulinaemia, a disorder that is characterised by excessive secretion of insulin from the beta-cells of the pancreas in the newborn and which is associated with severe hypoglycaemia.
the molecular genetics of congenital hyperinsulinaemia.

the proband has a de novo mosaic mutation (Q54x) and mosaic paternal uniparent isodisomy for chromosome 11, resulting in atypical histological CHI.
the proband's CHI resulted from a combination of mosaic paternal UPD and a paternally derived Q54X ABCC8 gene nonsense mutation.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a novel genetic mechanism of atypical diffuse congenial hyperinsulinism is due to mosaic uniparent isodisomy in a patient with dominantly inherited mutation in the ABCC8 gene.
atypical diffuse CHI is a mosaic disorder of UPD and that the mosaic nature of the UPD is due to an early postzygotic event.
a mosaic ABCC8 mutation and mosaic interstitial paternal UPD on chromosome 11p are responsible for an atypical form of CHI.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a patient with a diffuse pattern of beta-cell hyperplasia on histology, but without a clear focal lesion, should not be excluded from genetic testing.
the genetic mechanism of diffuse hyperinsulinism may be more complex than previously thought.
the genetic diagnosis of atypical diffuse hyperinsulinism can be challenging and requires careful molecular investigation of the pancreatic tissue.
